card.name: Subject noun just before a reported finding
card.fires_on: The noun or comma that ends the subject of a sentence reporting observed findings, right before the verb such as was, were or have been reported. Seen in adverse-event and trial-result passages.

modes.label: Patients in trial death rate
modes.description: The word patients after drug-treated, in the antipsychotic mortality warning, right before the rate figure.
modes.example: the rate of death in drug-treated<< patients>> was about 4.5%, compared

modes.label: Comma after a clause
modes.description: A comma closing an opening clause such as when available or when patients presented with elevated values, before the main finding.
modes.example: Histological findings, when available<<,>> were consistent with glomerular microangi

modes.label: Event noun before reported
modes.description: The end of a noun for an event or finding, just before have been reported or found.
modes.example: Road traffic<< accidents>> attributed to sudden sleep onset have been reported

card.writes: It slightly pushes toward words like nominal and away from hedges such as probably, likely and maybe, which fits plain factual reporting.
card.plain: It marks the point where a subject about observed findings is complete and the statement of what was found is about to follow.
